subject: Surge absorption capacity mapping for private GPU pools (ACME)
body:
--- Message 1/4 ---
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmeretail.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeretail.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-18 09:12 PDT
Subject: Private GPU pool: throughput & burst plan (ACME/Redwood)

Vanessa —

Thanks for taking this on. We're doing an internal readout next month and need a concrete, auditable plan for our private deployment (VPC, on-prem edge racks) that covers:
- Sustained throughput target for our baseline (expected normal traffic)
- Burst/surge headroom for marketing-led spikes (we have a recent example attached)
- Network egress/ingress constraints and recommended MTU/QoS settings
- Cold/warm cache behavior (KV cache pre-warm windows and eviction implications)
- A canary rollout checklist (sizing for canary vs prod)

Context: last holiday campaign produced a sharp spike around the email send and checkout flows — attached are sample logs (per-token timestamps). In short we need to support ~1.2M tokens/min sustained during peak weekday afternoons, but be able to absorb short bursts to ~2.5M tokens/min for 3–10 minute windows with minimal 95/99p latency impact. Our compliance team also needs to see explicit network egress limits and private link topology before we greenlight the VPC peering.

Can you outline a recommended capacity mapping and a short list of must-have network configs? Also include any short-lived policy recommendations (e.g., burst credits, preemption rules, KV eviction priorities).

Attachments: acme_capacity_spike_logs.csv

Thanks,
Samir
Director, Edge Engineering
ACME Retail

--- Message 2/4 ---
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmeretail.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-18 12:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: throughput & burst plan (ACME/Redwood)

Samir —

Appreciate the detail and logs. High-level recommendation (TL;DR up front):
- Baseline reserved pool: 12 x A100-80GB equiv GPUs dedicated to ACME in your VPC (sustained target ~1.2M tokens/min).
- Burst credit pool: additional 6 GPUs available as "burst credits" for short windows, up to ~2.5M tokens/min for 3–10 minute surges. Burst usage is metered and auto-reclaimed.
- Steady-state reserve: keep 20% of reserved capacity as warm-headroom for KV-cache cold-starts and routing churn.

Sizing rationale and math:
- Based on our microbenchmark, one A100-80GB equiv can serve ~95k short-form tokens/min at median latency for 32-token responses with 99th percentile tail ~140–160ms (workload dependent).
- 12 GPUs x 95k ≈ 1.14M tokens/min (rounded to 1.2M accounting for batching and small-model variance).
- Burst add: 6 GPUs x 95k ≈ 570k tokens/min -> combined peak ≈ 1.7M. We also rely on network-level admission and degraded-model fallback to reach the ~2.5M transient target (e.g., fall back to smaller quantized model with 1.4x higher throughput for tokens that can tolerate slightly lower quality).

Autoscale & policy suggestions:
- Metric: token-rate (tokens/sec) aggregated over 60s sliding window with a 30s smoothing factor to avoid flapping.
- Burst credits: token-budget ledger per day; credits consumed from credit pool when token-rate > baseline threshold. Credits auto-replenish overnight and can be topped up programmatically (useful for marketing ops to pre-buy burst credits for launches).
- Preemption: reserve lanes for SLA-critical traffic (checkout flows). Non-critical requests (e.g., exploratory chat sessions) admitted into best-effort lane and evicted first under pressure.
- KV cache: pre-warm window of 10–15 minutes before expected campaign start; use prefix-based warming for high-QPS keys. Eviction policy: LRU with priority tagging (tag checkout-related keys as high priority).

Networking (must-haves):
- PrivateLink/Private Service Connect for control-plane and metrics: no public egress for inference traffic.
- Node NICs: minimum 25Gbps per GPU host; recommend 100Gbps spine for racks handling >8 hosts.
- MTU: 9000 (jumbo frames) across the VPC to reduce CPU overhead on dataplane; verify switch and router support.
- QoS: DSCP markings for inference control traffic and checkout lanes.
- Egress caps: recommend per-subnet egress polic(ies) of 8–12 Gbps during steady-state with burst allowances; we'll enforce per-route quotas at the NLB layer to avoid noisy neighbor issues.

Canary plan (short):
- Canary fleet: 2 GPUs attached to customer's VPC with identical routing and lower traffic percentage (2–5%). Run 4-hour soak followed by 1-hour peak injection test (synthetic token spikes matching your logs).
- Observability: 99/95 latency histograms, token accounting, KV miss rates, and model fallback counts in console.

I attached a simple working model (redwood_surge_model_v1.xlsx) that steps through the math and simulates different burst patterns.

Next steps:
- If this matches expectations, we'll schedule a technical runbook session to validate network configs and a 48-hour canary window.
- Rishi / Jordan — can you run a short lab sim against the attached logs to calibrate the 95/99p numbers and confirm KV warm-up sensitivity? I'll prepare a draft canary checklist for Samir.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

--- Message 3/4 ---
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-19 09:30 PDT
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: throughput & burst plan (ACME/Redwood) — internal action items\n
Rishi / Jordan — quick internal checklist before we lock dates with ACME: 
1) Perf sims: run the attached ACME spike logs through our surge simulator (INF-1129). Target: validate 99p < 160ms and 95p < 120ms for the baseline config.
2) KV cache sensitivity: run test with 10, 15, and 30 minute pre-warm windows; report miss-rate delta and time-to-stabilize.
3) Eviction & preemption: implement a staged eviction test where checkout-tagged keys are protected; measure customer-perceived error rate when we trigger a 2x sustained overload.
4) Canary infra: build the two-GPU canary in dev VPC; verify PrivateLink+NLB and MTU 9000 end-to-end.
5) Network QoS: coordinate with SRE to reserve DSCP lanes and validate 25Gbps host NICs under synthetic load.

Owner / ETA: Rishi — perf sims & KV tests by 2028-04-22 COB. Jordan — canary infra + QoS validation by 2028-04-24. I'll consolidate results and share a 1-page runbook for ACME by 2028-04-25.

If anything looks risky we escalate to Infra Eng for an extra reserved spine capacity.

Thanks — Vanessa

--- Message 4/4 ---
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmeretail.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeretail.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-20 10:45 PDT
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: throughput & burst plan (ACME/Redwood)

Vanessa / team —

This looks great and is the level of detail our infra/compliance folks wanted. A few follow-ups:
- Can we get a 48-hour canary window in the week of 2028-05-08? Priya will coordinate blackout windows.
- Please include a short paragraph in the runbook about model fallback quality tradeoffs (which models we use as fallbacks and expected token-level quality delta).
- Compliance wants the network_topology.drawio included in the runbook (I attached a skeletal draft).

If you can get Rishi's sims by 4/22 and Jordan's validation by 4/24 as noted, we'll sign off and move to a DocuSign for a small burst-credit prepay.

Samir
Director, Edge Engineering | ACME Retail

--- End of thread ---
